language_wrapper: Let S = {1, 2, ..., {alpha}}. Consider unordered collections of {r} pairwise disjoint, nonempty subsets of S whose union has exactly {t} elements, and where each subset has size between {l} and {u}, inclusive. Two collections are considered the same if they differ only by reordering the subsets. Let N be the number of such collections. Compute N modulo {modulus}.
hardness_rationale: The seed counts unordered pairs of disjoint nonempty subsets of a fixed set and reduces to a simple 3^n-style argument followed by division by 2. Our augmentation requires counting unordered collections of r >= 2 disjoint nonempty subsets with additional lower/upper bounds on each subset’s size and a prescribed union size t. This forces a more advanced approach: first choose the t used elements, then count constrained set partitions with block sizes in [l,u]. The latter is not a direct Stirling-number evaluation unless l=1 and u is unbounded; instead it requires either exponential generating functions or a dedicated dynamic programming/inclusion-exclusion for labeled distributions followed by division by r!. The verifier enforces nontrivial constraints, ensuring the instance cannot be solved by the seed’s shortcut and demands careful combinatorial reasoning.
notes: The verifier computes the labeled distribution count via a DP recurrence F[i][j] = sum_{c=l..u} C(j,c) F[i-1][j-c], then divides by r! to obtain unlabeled partitions. It multiplies by C(alpha, t) to account for choosing which t elements from the ground set participate. Difficulty is enforced by avoiding the trivial (l==1 and u>=t) case and requiring multiple occupancy compositions.
source_question: Let $\mathcal{S}$ be the set $\lbrace1,2,3,\ldots,10\rbrace$ Let $n$ be the number of sets of two non-empty disjoint subsets of $\mathcal{S}$ . (Disjoint sets are defined as sets that have no common elements.) Find the remainder obtained when $n$ is divided by $1000$ .
